title: Morbi Ceramic Cluster
subtitle: From Traditional Craft to Global Manufacturing Hub

items.title: Traditional Craft Origins
items.desc: Clay roofing tiles (nalia), wall clocks, and local earthenware. A locally-rooted, labour-intensive, informal industry.

items.title: First Major Shift
items.desc: Transition from traditional products to modern ceramic tiles. Mosaic and galicha tiles replaced clay roofing as primary output.

items.title: The Game Changer
items.desc: Collective adoption of automation, digital printing & spool-roller tunnel firing — the defining technological turning point.

items.title: Global Standing
items.desc: High-end vitrified tiles, sanitaryware, and large-format slabs. India becomes the world's #2 ceramic tile producer.

items.label: Globally
items.qualifier: World's second-largest producer & consumer of ceramic tiles, trailing only China.

items.label: of India
items.qualifier: Morbi cluster alone produces 80–90% of India's total ceramic tile output.

items.label: Years Old
items.qualifier: A century of ceramic industrial heritage underpins Morbi's global reputation.

blocks.footnote: Trailing only China in global production scale

items.desc: Umbrella body enabling cooperation — fraud prevention, order-sharing via subcontracting, and unified representation to state authorities.
Patel-Prajapati networks foster mutual support during financial stress, enabling informal credit and minimising conflict.
Unified voice successfully secured GST cuts, anti-dumping duties, and infrastructure investments.
Dedicated gas pipelines, reliable power supply, road network linking to Kandla & Mundra ports for seamless export logistics.
Central government tariffs shield domestic manufacturers from low-cost Chinese imports and price undercutting.
Tax rate cut from 28% to 18% after industry protests, significantly boosting domestic consumption.

items.title: Global Competition
items.body: Chinese manufacturers with massive scale & lower costs pressure both domestic and export markets persistently.

items.title: Environmental Regulation
items.body: NGT ordered closure of coal gasifiers, forcing costly transition to LNG to reduce SO₂ and particulate pollution.

items.title: Labour Informality
items.body: Reliance on migrant & casual workers — dust hazards, no social security, no permanent employment status.

items.title: Urban Sprawl & Finance
items.body: Cash crunches + ribbon development, water scarcity, and unplanned land growth along highways.

items.title: Collective Reinvention
items.body: Technology adopted cluster-wide and across all the firms simultaneously.

items.title: Social Capital
items.body: Community trust networks enabled non-competitive cooperation — replicable only with deep social embeddedness.

items.title: Unresolved Tensions
items.body: Environment, labour formalisation & urban planning remain the defining challenges of the next chapter.
